# Klef

> Klef (klef.sh) is a personal, end-to-end encrypted tool for keeping .env
> files (by default .env.local and .env.production) in sync across machines.
> Files are encrypted with AES-256-GCM on the device, in the browser or the
> CLI, before upload; the server stores only ciphertext it cannot decrypt.
> The CLI never prints a secret value, so coding agents such as Claude Code
> and Cursor can run it. Free, open source (AGPL-3.0), and self-hostable.

Key facts:

- Zero-knowledge / end-to-end encrypted: the server never sees file contents,
  the master passphrase, the recovery key, or any decryption-capable key.
- Envelope encryption: a random per-account data encryption key (DEK) encrypts
  files; a key encryption key derived from the passphrase via Argon2id
  (19 MiB, t=2; PBKDF2-SHA-256 600k fallback) wraps the DEK.
- A 128-bit recovery key (KLEF-XXXXX-...) is shown exactly once at setup. If
  both the passphrase and the recovery key are lost, data is unrecoverable by
  design.
- Sign-in (Google, GitHub, or passkeys) is separate from unlocking, which
  happens entirely on the device. Auto-lock and manual lock clear keys from memory.
- Every save creates a new version, so files have history and restore.
- CLI (@klefsh/cli): `setup` signs in, links a repo, installs a Claude Code
  skill and a Cursor rule, and pulls missing files; `sync` pushes or pulls
  whichever side changed and stops on conflicts; `restore` pulls every linked
  checkout on a new machine; `audit` compares key names on Vercel, GitHub and
  Cloudflare with local files, read-only. No command prints a secret value,
  and the passphrase is read only from the terminal.
- No analytics, trackers, ads, or third-party scripts.
- Runs on Cloudflare Workers with D1; self-hostable on your own account.
- Built by Beny Dishon K (https://beny.one).
